Hi Samir / Aditya — looping in some concrete numbers from our initial sizing exercise (see notes below and attached high-level quote). This is still high level — we can refine after the deep-dive.

Sizing assumptions (baseline):
- Steady tokens/day (baseline): 35 req/s * 120 tokens * 86,400s/day ≈ 362M tokens/day (note: this is theoretical peak; we model sustained throughput at 35 req/s).
- Avg tokens/request baseline: 120

Cost comparison (very rough back-of-envelope):
- Hosted API (per-token): $0.00030 per completion token — at 362M tokens/day this scales quickly (example: 362M * $0.00030 ≈ $108.6k/day). Hosted is attractive for low-volume or bursty workloads but becomes expensive at sustained high volume.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): example pilot = 8x A10/RTX-class GPUs reserved for a committed monthly fee (includes software + autoscaling buffer). Rough committed price: $65k/month for the pilot config (ballpark) — amortized tokens/month can make $/token an order of magnitude lower vs hosted depending on utilization.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): one-time infra + integration + monthly support; economics depend heavily on customer infra costs and ops team. Typically highest up-front but lowest long-term if you own HW and run heavy sustained throughput.

Recommendations / next steps:
- For your stated priorities (latency, SOC2, US residency) Dedicated looks like the likely sweet spot for pilot → production.
- Next step: 30-min technical deep-dive (Marissa + Neha + Samir) to lock GPU sizing, burst policy, and run utilization sensitivity in the spreadsheet. After that we can produce a formal pilot quote (3-month commit) and a statement of work.
